_comment: Starter ontology for the ODE (Ontology-Directed Extraction) pipeline, scoped to Indian Supreme Court land/property-dispute judgments. Grounded in real text from the downloaded sample (see gold_examples.jsonl for the sentences this was built from), not designed in the abstract. Expect this to grow via the bootstrapping loop (Seed -> Lift -> Lower -> Audit -> Refine) -- residuals that don't fit an existing class are the signal for the next revision, not a reason to force-fit them.

ie_concepts.Claim: What a party asserts is true or owed to them (e.g. ownership, possession, right to recovery).
ie_concepts.Issue: The question the court frames itself as deciding.
ie_concepts.RuleCited: A statute, section, or article invoked as governing law.
ie_concepts.AuthorityCited: A prior case invoked as precedent.
ie_concepts.AuthorityTreatment: How the citing court treated an AuthorityCited -- see TreatmentAction polarity below. This is the signed-graph edge label.
ie_concepts.Fact: A fact the court treats as established in the record.
ie_concepts.Holding: The court's determination on an Issue.
ie_concepts.Outcome: The disposition of the case (appeal allowed/dismissed, application admitted, etc.).

terminology._comment: keyword/phrase -> class, lower-cased matching. This is what the LLM grounding step is seeded with; it is expected to be incomplete and grow from residuals.

known_gaps: The land-dispute filter (filtered_land_disputes.xlsx) sweeps in adjacent domains -- e.g. an income-tax case and an IBC/insolvency case turned up in the sample purely because immovable property was mortgaged as collateral. PropertyAsset needs a 'security_interest' sub-case, not just classic possession/title disputes.

AuthorityTreatment verbs (relied on/distinguished/etc.) are reliable for pre-2000 judgments via the HEADNOTE section, but post-2000 judgments don't use that convention -- the same treatment is expressed in free text ('We are of the view that the said judgment would not even remotely be applicable...' = a distinguishing, with no verb from the list at all). This is exactly the gap the modern-case sign classifier (classify_modern_signs.py) targets.

RulingAction+Patient was found (via LEARN, 2026-09-18) to be ambiguous across Holding/RuleCited/Outcome/AuthorityCited -- 'held that X' means different things depending on what X contains. Split DispositionAction out for the Outcome case (appeal allowed/dismissed/admitted). The remaining Holding-vs-RuleCited ambiguity (does X state a determination or invoke a statute?) still needs a content-based rule, not just a class split, since both use the same 'held' trigger.
